subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & Context-Length Profiling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@acme.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Pricing & Context-Length Profiling

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a short list of items that'll help us scope pricing and the right deployment option (hosted vs. dedicated/private).

Call recap:
- Primary use: customer-facing summarization + assisted workflows (search + generate).
- Current traffic: low production volume today, piloting with ~100K monthly active users.
- Key constraints: latency SLOs ~ <300ms p95 for API flows; strict data controls for PII.

To price accurately we need a short token & context profile from you. Can you share the following by EOD Tuesday?
- Average prompt tokens (typical user prompt)
- Average completion tokens (expected response length)
- Monthly token volumes (prompts and completions) or per-user estimate
- Percentage of queries that need >8k, >32k, and >128k context
- Target budget or target $/1M tokens if you have one (helps us propose a blended price)

Next steps we propose:
1) You send the token profile CSV (sample attached would be perfect).
2) We map to 8k/32k/128k profiles and propose a blended pricing model + reserved capacity options.
3) 30-min follow-up next week to walk numbers and recommended rollout.

Attachment: token profile template (see attached).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
--Attachment: token_profile_template.csv (stub)

Date: 2026-03-26T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & Context-Length Profiling

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. Below is the token/context profile from our preliminary logs (exported from our staging). I've attached the CSV for the raw samples.

Summary (most likely production pattern):
- Avg prompt tokens: 420 tokens (UI prompts + metadata)
- Avg completion tokens: 1,200 tokens (concise but multi-paragraph summaries)
- Monthly estimate (pilot -> prod): currently 8M prompt tokens / 24M completion tokens; expecting 20M prompts / 60M completions in 6 months at scale
- Context-length needs: ~70% of queries fit within 8k, ~25% require up to 32k (long threads + doc context), ~5% need 128k for full-doc summarization or entire legal docs
- Target budget: looking to hit approximately $1,500 per 1M tokens as a blended goal (open to tradeoffs for higher context windows)

Attachment: acme-token-profile.csv (sample rows included).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@acme.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-27T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & Context-Length Profiling

Samira — this is super helpful, thanks for the detail and the CSV. A few quick notes and a proposed pricing structure so you have something concrete to review ahead of the call.

What I ran quickly against your profile:
- Weighted avg tokens per call (prompt + completion): ~1,620 tokens
- Projected monthly tokens at scale: ~80M tokens (20M prompts + 60M completions)
- Context mix: 70% 8k, 25% 32k, 5% 128k

Pricing options (provisional):
1) Hosted, usage-based (no commit):
   - 8k context: $1,800 per 1M tokens
   - 32k context: $2,400 per 1M tokens
   - 128k context: $3,600 per 1M tokens
   - Blended example (using your mix): ~ $1,920 per 1M tokens

2) Reserved / Dedicated (6\u201312 month commit) \u2014 recommended at your target scale to get unit economics closer to target $1,500/1M:
   - Base blended: $1,500 per 1M tokens with a 30\u201350% reserved commit depending on peak usage and QPS guarantees
   - Priority capacity, predictable latency SLOs, optional model pinning for auditability

Notes & questions:
- Can you confirm expected peak QPS and concurrency for busiest flows? That impacts whether we recommend dedicated shards vs. hosted autoscaling.
- For the ~5% 128k traffic, are these one-off batch jobs (can be queued) or user-facing interactive flows that require sub-second latency? If they can be batched, we can recommend queued jobs on dedicated infra at lower marginal cost.

I've attached a short PDF mapping your profile to cost scenarios and included a recommended reserved-capacity proposal for 6- and 12-month terms. Would you be open to a 30-min review on Thu 3/29 9:30 AM PT?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
--Attachment: redwood-pricing-vs-usage.pdf (type: application/pdf, 210 KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & Context-Length Profiling (internal note)

Internal only quick note summarizing recommended commercial approach before the Thu call. Do not reply-all to external until we align on concession levels.

Key facts from Acme: target blended $1,500 / 1M, projected ~80M tokens/month at scale, context mix 70/25/5 (8k/32k/128k).

Recommendation:
- Offer a 6-month reserved agreement that gets them to ~$1,500/1M blended with the following structure: 40% committed usage at a 35% discount to hosted list, remaining on-demand at a smaller discount.
- For 128k traffic (5%), propose a separate queued batch tier priced at higher per-1M but with efficient resource allocation; this keeps interactive unit cost low and avoids blowing the blended metric.
- Include an SLA-based upsell for priority capacity + model pinning as a line item.

Action items:
- Marissa: confirm whether Acme's 128k queries are interactive. If batchable, we include batching language in the proposal.
- Jordan: prepare DRAFT term sheet with 6-month and 12-month reserved options and shortfall/overage language.
- I'll prep an internal cost model showing blended $/1M at different reserved % levels for the call.

I'll join the call on Thu.

-Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
